fields.test_cases_present: partial - both specs describe protocol-compliance requirements and waveforms that map directly to compliance test scenarios but neither provides a formal verification plan.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: Reset behavior
scenarios: HRESETn LOW: all Manager outputs in defined state (HTRANS=IDLE recommended).
HRESETn HIGH: first valid transfer issued no earlier than the first rising HCLK after HRESETn=HIGH.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: Single NONSEQ transfer
scenarios: Read and write SINGLE bursts with HTRANS=NONSEQ at start, HTRANS=IDLE after.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: IDLE transfer must return zero-wait OKAY
scenarios: Subordinate sampled on HTRANS=IDLE returns HREADYOUT=1, HRESP=OKAY, ignores transfer.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: BUSY transfer must return zero-wait OKAY
scenarios: Subordinate sampled on HTRANS=BUSY returns HREADYOUT=1, HRESP=OKAY, ignores transfer.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: Incrementing bursts INCR4 / INCR8 / INCR16
scenarios: Sequence: NONSEQ + (length-1) * SEQ; address increments by 2^HSIZE bytes.
INCR (undefined length): NONSEQ + N * SEQ + IDLE or NONSEQ-to-new-burst termination.
Must NOT cross 1KB address boundary.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: Wrapping bursts WRAP4 / WRAP8 / WRAP16
scenarios: Sequence: NONSEQ + (length-1) * SEQ; address wraps at length*2^HSIZE bytes.
HBURST and HSIZE constant across burst.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: 1KB burst boundary enforcement
scenarios: INCR burst that would cross 1KB must be rejected/split by Manager.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: Subordinate wait-state insertion
scenarios: Subordinate drives HREADYOUT=LOW for N cycles, then HIGH; Manager holds address-phase signals on the next transfer.
Manager must restrict HTRANS changes during waited transfers (IDLE→NONSEQ, BUSY→SEQ/other) per Section 3.7.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: Two-cycle ERROR response
scenarios: Subordinate drives HRESP=1+HREADY=0 then HRESP=1+HREADY=1.
Manager option A: continue burst.
Manager option B: drive HTRANS=IDLE during the 2-cycle ERROR to cancel.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: Locked transfer sequence
scenarios: Manager asserts HMASTLOCK across a read+write sequence to the same address (SWP-like).
All transfers in the locked sequence to the same Subordinate region.
IDLE transfer recommended after a locked sequence.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: HPROT and burst-constant signals
scenarios: HSIZE, HBURST, HWRITE, HPROT, HMASTLOCK, HNONSEC remain constant for all beats of a burst.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: Default Subordinate
scenarios: Access to unmapped address returns ERROR (NONSEQ/SEQ) or zero-wait OKAY (IDLE/BUSY).

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: Write strobes (Issue C optional)
scenarios: Sparse write: HWSTRB byte lanes selectively HIGH; LOW lanes are inactive.
On read: HWSTRB should be deasserted.
Across beats of a burst: HWSTRB may change.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: AHB5 Exclusive access
scenarios: Exclusive read with HEXCL=1 + HMASTER=I records monitor at (Addr, I); HEXOKAY=1.
Exclusive write same HMASTER returns HEXOKAY=1 if monitor still valid; HEXOKAY=0 if another Manager wrote in between.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: AHB5 Secure transfers
scenarios: HNONSEC must remain constant throughout a burst.
Secure (HNONSEC=0) vs Non-secure (HNONSEC=1) accesses handled by Subordinate.

derived_compliance_test_categories_ahb.name: AHB5 Interface protection via parity
scenarios: Inject single-bit fault on HADDR; HADDRCHK mismatches; error detected and signaled to integrator-defined error indicator.

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: Reset behavior
scenarios: PRESETn LOW: PSELx=0, PENABLE=0 (IDLE).
PRESETn HIGH: first SETUP no earlier than next rising PCLK.

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: Write transfer no wait states
scenarios: SETUP -> ACCESS -> IDLE; PADDR + PWRITE + PSEL + PWDATA stable; PREADY=1 in ACCESS.

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: Write transfer with wait states
scenarios: ACCESS with PREADY=0 for N cycles; all bridge outputs stable; PREADY=1 completes transfer.

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: Read transfer no wait states
scenarios: SETUP -> ACCESS -> IDLE; PADDR + PWRITE + PSEL stable; PRDATA driven before end of ACCESS; PREADY=1.

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: Read transfer with wait states
scenarios: ACCESS with PREADY=0 for N cycles; bridge outputs stable.

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: Failing write transfer (PSLVERR=1)
scenarios: PSLVERR=1 in the cycle PREADY=1; peripheral may or may not have updated its register.

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: Failing read transfer (PSLVERR=1)
scenarios: PSLVERR=1 in the cycle PREADY=1; PRDATA may return invalid data (no requirement to drive zero).

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: PSLVERR valid window
scenarios: PSLVERR only valid when PSEL=PENABLE=PREADY=1; LOW recommended at other times.

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: PSELx mutual exclusion
scenarios: Only one PSELx asserted per transfer; bridge ensures decode.

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: Write strobes (APB4 only)
scenarios: Sparse write: PSTRB byte lanes selectively HIGH on write; ALL LOW on read.
PSTRB[n] -> PWDATA[(8n+7):8n].

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: Protection (APB4 only)
scenarios: Normal vs privileged (PPROT[0]).
Secure vs non-secure (PPROT[1]).
Data vs instruction (PPROT[2]).
PPROT must remain stable during wait states.

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: AHB-to-APB bridge end-to-end
scenarios: AHB write hits APB peripheral; bridge converts HADDR + HWDATA into PADDR + PWDATA + PSELx + PENABLE.
APB PSLVERR maps back to AHB HRESP=ERROR.

derived_compliance_test_categories_apb.name: AXI-to-APB bridge end-to-end
scenarios: APB PSLVERR maps back to AXI RRESP/BRESP=SLVERR.

evidence.quote: Subordinates must always provide a zero wait state OKAY response to IDLE transfers and the transfer must be ignored by the Subordinate. Same for BUSY.
Managers must not attempt to start an incrementing burst that crosses a 1KB address boundary. All transfers in a burst must be aligned to the address boundary equal to the size of the transfer.
Subordinates use HREADYOUT to insert wait states. The Manager is restricted to what changes it can make to the transfer type and address during a waited transfer.
ERROR response is a two-cycle response on HRESP.
Default Subordinate returns ERROR for NONSEQ/SEQ, zero-wait OKAY for IDLE/BUSY.
Exclusive Access Monitor; HEXCL + HMASTER + HEXOKAY.
Parity check signals provide single-bit fault detection on each interface.
Setup phase one cycle, Access phase one or more cycles (PREADY-controlled).
PSLVERR is only considered valid during the last cycle of an APB transfer, when PSEL, PENABLE, and PREADY are all HIGH.
